cell_dimensions.cover_screw: 8-32 x 5/8 in socket head cap screw (15.9 mm), 8 per enclosure
cell_dimensions.seat_screw: 8-32 x 2 in socket head cap screw (50.8 mm) through the lid and the lower half, 2 per seat
cell_dimensions.holder: V9.7 split sliding enclosure: plain block, lower half + lid + 2 covers in an 11.3 mm pocket, two through-slot screws (one per end), closed stem pocket
notes: Local frame: x along the bore and the beam, y across (sliding direction), z up; origin on the bore axis at the middle of the cell; the parting plane z = 0 is the 12.7 mm optical axis.

Cell per Thorlabs drawing 24088-E0W (GC25075-RB): dia 25.4 x 71.8 (tolerances 0.3 / 0.8), fill stem at mid-length, stem height 10 mm MAX; the stem diameter is not on the drawing (6.3 assumed for display).

Plain rectangular block 88 x 46.9 x 48 (x = +-44), nothing protrudes. Bore 30.4 mm = cell 25.4 + 5, through the whole length, bored with the two halves clamped together; the cell is centred in the bore by the heater/insulation (not modelled), which must also keep it from sliding along the bore.

Two through slots (4.37 wide, screw centres y = 0.5 .. 11, both halves) at x = +-39.9 in the bore's end regions, 1.0 mm beyond the cell end at its +0.8 tolerance and 1.9 mm inside the end faces; they lie in the local +y half of the bore while the beam uses the centre and the local -y half, so the screws never meet the cell or the beam.

Travel 10.5 mm toward local +y (board -x on the lattice board): beam through the cell centre at 0, 2.2 mm inside the cell wall at 10.5; the pocket wall on that side is the travel stop (1 mm clearance). In the body frame the screws move from y = 11 (centred) to y = 0.5 (full travel).
Two 8-32 x 2 in screws, one per end, from the lid top through the slots of both halves into the plate taps clamp the halves and fix the position; their heads ride in the lid's 8.5 x 5 counter-slots.
Stem pocket 12 x 10 split 5/5 by the parting plane, from the bore to 24.2 from the axis and CLOSED: 1.5 mm beyond the 10 mm MAX stem, 2.5 mm of wall to the outer face.
Cable notch 6 x 6 in the lower half's parting face through the local +y wall at x = -20.

Covers 7 mm thick, no beam aperture yet (to be opened later; the beam-passage audit exempts them explicitly). Cover holes at y = +17 / -14.5, z = +/-17: the +y pair clears the slots by 2.1 mm. The socket heads stand 0.9 mm proud of the 3.5 mm counterbores.
Cover taps 16 mm deep from each end face (two in each half); 5/8 in screws through the counterbored covers engage 12.4 mm and tie the halves together.

limitations: Bounding-box overlap alone is not evidence of physical collision.

Mesh candidates receive triangle BVH/SAT contact and closed-shell containment checks. Contacts include touching and crossing; no exact common mesh solid-volume assertion is made. Open shells or runtime limits remain explicit unresolved cases.
Part surfaces are tessellated with 0.04 mm deflection for ray intersection.
Finite-beam screening samples the center plus 8 azimuths at 50% and 100% radius; gaps between samples are not certified.
V5 uses explicitly supplied elliptical radii and piecewise straight marginal rays. Focus vertices, beam diameter, M-squared and cylindrical-axis orientation are layout assumptions, not measurements.
TA input is assumed 5 mm by 5/3 mm in 1/e^2 diameter; nominal 1:3 cylindrical and 1:2 spherical reduction gives 5/6 mm round diameter. External TA input is assumed already round with 5/3 mm diameter.
AOM entrance is approximately collimated; the 75 mm cat-eye lens focuses toward the return mirror. There is no f150 AOM entrance lens in V5.
Nominal CAD ray checks do not include RF-dependent diffraction or arbitrary alignment travel. Cable/front access projection and nominal output order separation are reported separately.

AOM root contacts are omitted only inside the measured 3 mm bore channel; each opening and the 1.5 x 2.5 mm active aperture are checked separately. Other expected root housing passages are listed; mounts and knobs remain in the ray checks.
The AOM active aperture is assumed centered on the CAD housing bore; the manufacturer specification is not a measured crystal-to-housing alignment tolerance.
Original platform fastener solids are included as separate assemblies; wrench/tool access is not certified.
Transparent optics are exempt only on their intended centered optical axis; side and rim contacts remain checked. No refraction, polarization, power, thermal or Gaussian mode-matching certification.
UI visibility never removes installed hardware from checks; only explicit installation-mode exclusions do.

isolator_input_check.scope: Nominal TA input route and CAD axis, not measured isolator forward transmission.

pbs_paths.scope: Nominal PBS T/R paths and actual CAD cue orientation; no polarization or physical transmission certification
pbs_paths.formula: a_norm = yaw + 180 + Proxy.reflection_angle; R = 2*a_norm - incoming - 180; T = incoming (degrees)
pbs_paths.cad_cue_formula: Diagonal slot tangent = yaw - Proxy.reflection_angle, from original cube_splitter.execute

orthogonal_paths.scope: All nominal axes must run along board X or Y; free-space crossings are allowed. Segments of a path that declares diffraction_kink_deg (the +1-order axis after an AOM) are exempt when they lie exactly at that angle from the board axes.

dual_leakage_interception_check.scope: Single TA or partial assembly without the main splitter.

output_optics.scope: Unfolded thin-lens paraxial feasibility screening at nominal RF; not a certified stray-light, measured Gaussian mode-match, or full diffracted-ray simulation.
limitations: The initial waist size and plane are assumptions; real TA M2 and output fiber mode must be measured.
The relative unwanted order is assumed to leave the return AOM aperture at the nominal single-order separation.
PBS refraction, lens aberrations, clipping before the iris, finite RF scan, and 3D diffraction-plane transformations are not included.
Available iris adjustment range and heater/cable dimensions remain independent mechanical checks.

The cable corridor starts 0.5 mm (configurable) beyond the furthest owning-hardware tail extent and stops at the board edge.
UI-hidden hardware is checked unless explicitly absent in this installation mode.
